key_insight: Factual recall in LLMs follows a sigmoid relationship driven by a log-linear combination of model parameter count and topic frequency in the training data; these two factors alone explain roughly 60% of recall variance.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a scaling law linking factual recall (and predictable confabulation) to both model size and the composition/representation of topics in training corpora, making recall more predictable across models and topics.
method: Automated reference-verification evaluation of 38 models on >8,900 scholarly references to measure factual recall quality.
Statistical modeling showing recall quality maps to a sigmoid function of a log-linear combination of model parameter count and topic representation in training data.
Quantified explanatory power (≈60% of variance) across a subset of dense models to validate the relationship.
impact: Provides a simple, quantitative rule linking model size and data coverage to factual recall, enabling practitioners to predict and mitigate confabulation by choosing model/data trade-offs and prioritizing topic coverage in training or retrieval.
visual_elements: Sigmoid curve plot: y-axis = recall quality, x-axis = log-linear combination of model size and topic frequency (annotated inflection point).
Heatmap/contour over model size vs. topic frequency showing regions of high vs. low factual recall.
Bar or pie chart summarizing variance explained (~60%) by the two-factor model compared to other factors.
Pipeline diagram: models → automated reference verification → statistical fit → actionable guidelines (icons for models, dataset, metrics).
paper_title: Predictable Confabulations: Factual Recall by LLMs Scales with Model Size and Topic Frequency
paper_authors: Matthew L. Smith, Jonathan P. Shock, Samuel T. Segun, Iyiola E. Olatunji, Tegawendé F. Bissyandé
